Dated this the 7th day of October, 2025 The petitioner is the de facto complainant in C.C.
No.116/2022 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-II, Harippad, which arose out of Crime No.138/2022 of Harippad Police Station, Alappuzha.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-II, Harippad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Respondents 3 to 5 are the accused Nos.1 to 3 in the aforesaid crime.

The offences alleged against them are under Sections 498A and 323 r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
2.
In the present petition, the petitioner would contend that the issue involved in this case has been amicably settled with respondents 3 to 5, and hence the proceedings against them are to be quashed.
3. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned counsel for respondents 3 to 5 and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.

4. The petitioner/de facto complainant has filed an affidavit before this Court stating that all the issues between her and respondents 3 to 5 have been amicably settled, and hence there is no need to continue the prosecution against respondents 3 to 5.
2025:KER:74469 5.

The learned Public Prosecutor, upon instructions, submitted that the petitioner/de facto complainant had given a statement to the Investigating Officer also to the effect that the matter has been amicably settled with respondents 3 to 5, and that she is not at all interested in continuing the prosecution against respondents 3 to 5.
6.

It appears that the dispute involved is purely of private nature, and no purpose would be fulfilled by the continuance of the prosecution in this case, and hence it is highly necessary to terminate the prosecution proceedings to prevent abuse of process of court.
Such a course is also required to maintain the harmonious relationship between the parties.

Therefore, the request in the present Varsha .G vs State Of Kerala on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50935638/
2 petition to quash the proceedings against respondents 3 to 5, has to be allowed.

sentences.text: In the result, the petition stands allowed.

The proceedings against respondents 3 to 5 (accused Nos.1 to 3) in C.C. No.116/2022 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-II, Harippad,
which arose out of Crime No.138/2022 of Harippad Police Station, Alappuzha, are hereby quashed.
